text: A man sent me a DM today that says, one of your videos mentions understanding male privilege, and I'd like to get to understand it myself better. Can you explain what you mean by male privilege and how it applies? Of course, male privilege comprises invisible advantages and rights that men automatically earn just because they exist in our society. And it's invisible, and that's why a lot of men don't recognize the privilege, because these are so deeply ingrained in the very fabric of the system in which we all live. So this guy made a video explaining the male privilege. Later, he goes into more details. And look, I actually don't have a problem with the idea that men can have certain advantages simply because they're a man. But here's what I do have a problem with. In the comments, he claims that female privilege doesn't exist. Wait, what? So you can recognize that men have advantages based on their sex, but somehow the idea that women might have advantages too is completely inconceivable? All right, let's talk about female advantages. And let me be clear, this isn't about competing over who has it worse. It is simply to show that men aren't the only ones who have advantages. Women, on average, live significantly longer than men. In the United States, almost five years longer. They also have lower mortality rates from many major causes of death. Women are significantly less likely to be murdered. Worldwide, only about 19% of homicide victims are female. And in the US, women have a suicide death rate that's roughly one quarter that of men. Women are also much less likely to work in dangerous and physically demanding occupations. In fact, only about 8% of fatal workplace injuries in the United States involve women. Now, how about dating? Women are generally more likely to be approached, asked out, and have someone else plan and pay for their dates. And women also receive significantly more romantic attention on dating apps. For example, a study published in 2019 found that women received approximately four times as many first messages as men. And the 2025 study found that even highly desirable men generally receive fewer expressions of interest than women who were below average in desirability on the platform studied. Now, how about education and employment? Women are now overrepresented in higher education across OECD countries, including among bachelor's and master's graduates. And on top of that, women have access to scholarships, university programs, and even additional university admission seats, specifically because they're women. For example, India's prestigious engineering institutes have additional admission seats reserved for female applicants. Germany has a government-funded program specifically designed to increase the number of female professors. And certain companies are legally required to meet gender quotas on their boards. And remember how we constantly hear about discrimination against women when applying for jobs? Well, a major meta-analysis covering more than 360,000 job applications found that discrimination against female applicants for traditionally male and gender-balanced jobs had largely disappeared in the more recent studies. But discrimination against male applicants for traditionally female jobs remained. And according to the latest U.S. employment figures, women accounted for approximately 92% of net payroll job growth over the previous year. And how about legal advantages? In the United States, women are exempt from registering for potential military conscription, while men are legally required to do so. In Germany, unmarried women automatically receive parental custody when their child is born, while fathers don't automatically receive joint custody. And according to the U.S. Sentencing Commission, women receive federal criminal sentences that are, on average, approximately 29% shorter than men's, even after statistical adjustments for relevant factors. And I could keep going. No, seriously, I'm not exaggerating when I say that while preparing for this video, I was collecting material, and I kid you not, I ended up with pages and pages of such examples. But here's the thing. My point isn't to turn this into some competition over which gender has it worse. I'm sure you could also put together pages and pages of research showing areas where men have advantages and women face disadvantages. And not every difference I've mentioned is necessarily evidence of discrimination. Some are legal advantages, some are social expectations, and some are simply differences in outcomes. But that's precisely my point. Both men and women have advantages. Both men and women have struggles. And most of the problems we're talking about aren't even exclusive to one gender. They affect both men and women, just at different rates, in different ways, or under different circumstances. In other words, our experiences are much more similar than some people would have you believe. And that's my problem with videos and comments like this. Instead of acknowledging that both genders face challenges and both enjoy certain advantages, we get these incredibly one-sided narratives where one gender apparently has all the privilege and the other has none. And I genuinely don't understand how someone can be so eager to recognize gender-based advantages in one direction while completely denying that they could exist in the other.
